best_for: Mac and Windows users who work with files on SFTP servers, S3 buckets or cloud drives and want them to show up as a normal disk in Finder or File Explorer.
description:
Mountain Duck is a disk-mounting app from iterate GmbH, the Swiss company behind the open source Cyberduck file transfer app, which Mountain Duck is built on.

Search the files on your server with Spotlight on a Mac or Windows Search on a PC, just like your own files. When you open an Office document from a shared server, Mountain Duck can lock it so a coworker does not overwrite your changes. On versioned Amazon S3 buckets you can open or roll back an earlier version of a file. An Activity panel shows running syncs and lets you cancel them, and you can create sharing links for files in Dropbox, Google Drive, OneDrive and Nextcloud. SFTP connections can reuse your existing OpenSSH settings.

points.title: Remote storage as a local disk
points.text: Mountain Duck mounts servers and cloud storage in Finder or File Explorer, so any app can open remote files. It speaks FTP, SFTP, WebDAV, SMB, S3, Azure, Google Cloud Storage, Backblaze B2, Dropbox, Google Drive, OneDrive, SharePoint, Box and Nextcloud.

points.title: Online-only files, offline when needed
points.text: Smart synchronization lists every remote file without downloading it, fetches files when opened and uploads in the background. Folders you mark stay available offline.

points.title: Encrypted vaults
points.text: It can open Cryptomator vaults, so files are encrypted on your machine before they reach the server.

points.title: Paid, per user, per major version
points.text: There is a free trial. A license covers one user on any number of computers, but only for one major version; later majors are a discounted upgrade. Cyberduck key holders and academic users get 30% off. The buy page lists prices in euros only, so none are quoted here.

points.title: Windows install details
points.text: The Windows app is an MSIX package that installs without administrator rights, but app sideloading must be allowed, which some managed PCs block. The online and smart sync modes need a file system driver that Windows asks to install on first connect.

points.title: Version 5 needs newer systems
points.text: Mountain Duck 5 needs macOS 13 or Windows 10 version 1809 or later. Older licenses and systems can use older releases; version 3.0.1 still ran on Windows 7. The Windows listing keeps 46 versions; macOS lists only the current release.
